title: Double helix numbers
back: Antiparallel, right-handed; purine always faces pyrimidine, so the width stays constant.

title: Length of DNA
back: Human diploid: 6.6 × 10⁹ bp → about 2.2 m. E. coli: 4.6 × 10⁶ bp → about 1.36 mm.

title: Nucleosome
legend: histones = rich in lysine, arginine (+ charge)
back: Beads-on-string chromatin; H1 and NHC proteins pack it further. Euchromatin active, heterochromatin inactive.

title: Hershey–Chase
back: Infect → blend → centrifuge. Radioactive phosphorus in the bacteria proves DNA is the genetic material.

title: Meselson–Stahl
back: E. coli in ¹⁵N then ¹⁴N; CsCl density gradient. Proves semiconservative replication.

title: Replication fork
back: Polymerase works only 5′→3′: leading strand continuous, lagging strand in Okazaki fragments joined by ligase.

title: Transcription unit
back: Promoter → structural gene → terminator. Template 3′→5′; coding strand 5′→3′ has the RNA's sequence.

title: hnRNA processing
back: Splicing removes introns; capping adds methyl guanosine triphosphate; tailing adds 200–300 A residues.

title: Genetic code
back: Triplet, unambiguous, degenerate, continuous (commaless), nearly universal.

title: Lac operon
back: i → repressor binds operator (off). Lactose (inducer) inactivates the repressor → z, y, a transcribed. Negative regulation.

title: HGP numbers
back: Chromosome 1 has most genes (2968), Y fewest (231); dystrophin is the largest gene.

title: DNA fingerprinting
back: Uses polymorphic satellite DNA (VNTRs). Forensics, paternity disputes, population studies.

title: Stop codons
back: U Are Away, U Are Gone, U Go Away. No tRNA exists for them; a release factor binds instead.
